findingResolution.assessment: The specific r3 omissions are corrected: K12 excludes backslash and limits scalar segments, K6 reader admission uses retained pinned censuses and drops nonmembers without rewriting/echoing, all grammars including items 2/3/5 now require whole decoded matches, identities retain their true-end patterns, and input encoded V is checked. The new blanket suffix refusal is a separate regression, SOP2-R4-03; complete predicate consistency is therefore not yet acceptable.

The original terminal-CAS-then-counter gap is removed for ordinary writer outcomes by one cumulative snapshot exchange, and producer drops commit by a single tally increment. Reading F before snapshots/enqueues/drops covers the requested failed-reservation and between-two-sinks gaps as outstanding calls. The bounded per-sink design is accepted. The pre-scope handoff still lacks disjoint accounting (SOP2-R4-01), and marker admission is not reconciled with its attempted CAS (SOP2-R4-02). The post-freeze required-envelope-write limitation remains accepted.

requiredFindings.title: Partition pre-scope and file accounting across the handoff

location.section: item 16 stage enqueue tallies, file snapshot taken count and freeze derivation; C-7

requiredFindings.problem: The pre-scope-to-file handoff has no disjoint accounting rule. Step 5 subtracts all file outcomes from the file enqueue tally, then also charges pre-scope entries not present in the file snapshot taken count to file drain-abandoned. A transferred entry can therefore be charged twice. Excluding pre-scope entries from the file enqueue tally instead makes the ordinary file subtraction negative after their file outcomes are published, unless the file snapshot outcomes are explicitly partitioned. The accepted bounded per-sink design can express the partition; the current equations do not.

evidence.note: A buffered entry is taken into the file when the invocation later holds the write capability.
Every stage has an enqueue tally; file snapshots include outcomes and a pre-scope taken count. Enqueue must precede any corresponding snapshot outcome.
Snapshots are read before tallies. Both the file pending subtraction and the pre-scope pending subtraction contribute file drain-abandoned.

One pre-scope enqueue P=1 is handed to file with E_file=1 before its push. Pause before the file snapshot exchange, so O_file=0 and T_taken=0. The stated subset invariant holds. The two bullets derive (1-0)+(1-0)=2 file abandonments for one file projection. If the handoff does not increment E_file and the file snapshot later publishes written=1/taken=1, the first subtraction becomes 0-1=-1.
The proposal promises exactly one count for each missed sink projection, including pauses before snapshot publication.

requiredFindings.fix: Specify whether file enqueue/outcome tallies contain transferred pre-scope records, and derive a disjoint total from bounded cells. One option is to partition direct-file and pre-scope terminal outcomes in the same atomic file snapshot, subtract direct outcomes only from direct enqueues, and subtract pre-scope terminal outcomes only from pre-scope enqueues; taking a record into an intermediate queue must not erase its pending disposition. Another option is one combined file incoming total against all file outcomes, without adding the pre-scope pending entries again. Define the no-file-capability unpersisted case and each handoff pause so the total remains nonnegative and exactly one per file projection. Add a C-7 pause across the handoff, before the atomic taken/outcome publication, with one buffered record and a frozen/final-envelope file loss count of exactly one. Retain the accepted bounded cells; no per-record history is requested.

requiredFindings.title: Reconcile marker gate admission with its attempted CAS

location.section: item 17 marker state machine and syscall admission point; item 16 freeze; C-7

requiredFindings.problem: The marker gate load is explicitly its syscall admission point, but recording attempted requires a subsequent CAS on a different cell. The finalizer can change not-attempted to skipped in that gap. An admitted pre-freeze marker with no recorded completion is then reported skipped, despite the stated unconfirmed meaning covering that case. The initial attempted CAS loser path is not defined, so the text also does not determine whether the marker syscall is still issued after the finalizer wins. Completion-CAS handling alone does not settle this admission race.

evidence.note: At the freeze, not-attempted becomes skipped and attempted becomes unconfirmed.

Admission is through the ordinary gate; attempted is a separate CAS. Skipped means never attempted before freeze; unconfirmed means admitted with completion not recorded by freeze. The explicit loser rule speaks of a writer outcome after freeze.
The acquire load of open is the syscall admission point, including for the marker. A previously admitted unit may issue after closure.

Drain and encode marker; acquire-load gate=open; pause before not-attempted->attempted CAS; finalizer closes gate and CASes not-attempted->skipped; resume writer. The initial CAS loses, while admission occurred before freeze and no completion was recorded.
C-7 covers a stalled marker write and observing the five outcomes, but not the gap between its successful gate load and attempted CAS.

requiredFindings.fix: Give the marker a complete bounded publication/state protocol, including what happens when its initial attempted or suppressed CAS loses to finalization. Align the observable outcome meanings with that protocol. If admission remains the separate gate load, skipped must mean no attempt/admission was recorded in the cell by freeze, with the pre-freeze-load uncertainty expressly stated; it cannot prove that admission or an attempt never occurred. Alternatively coordinate logical attempt publication and admission so the stated skipped/unconfirmed distinctions follow. Specify whether a losing initial CAS aborts the syscall or becomes permitted post-freeze activity, consistently with the existing gate and S-OP-7 residual ownership. Add the exact load-to-attempted-CAS pause to C-7 and check the frozen state, any subsequent syscall, and the post-freeze tally. Do not restore a physical-syscall-return test for unconfirmed.

requiredFindings.title: Apply whole-value matching without banning lawful path suffixes

location.section: item 13c common whole-value/no-trimming rule; K12; r4 response table; C-4/C-5

requiredFindings.problem: The new common rule refuses a trailing LF, CR or space for every string grammar. LogicalPath permits those code points, including at the end of a normal segment. K12 explicitly inherits LogicalPath, and rule E can safely encode these names. Thus lawful admitted project paths such as a followed by a space, LF or CR are rejected by the common rule, contradicting K12 and C-5. Whole-value matching rejects a suffix only when that suffix is outside the particular grammar; a true-end assertion does not remove characters from an otherwise permissive path grammar. The cited identity law applies its suffix prohibition to identifiers, not every path.

evidence.note: The response table states the same general trailing-whitespace refusal as the operative common rule.
The rule is under Common rules and Every grammar, without a K12 exception.
K12 paths inherit LogicalPath; neither its path nor elided-tail predicate excludes trailing space/LF/CR.
The pinned LogicalPath excludes slash, backslash and NUL within normal segments, and dot/dot-dot components. Space, LF and CR are permitted within or at the end of a segment.
The cited trailing-LF/CR/space refusal concerns ExecutionId and RequestId grammars.
Rule E emits LF/CR as six ASCII escape characters and elision preserves code-point suffixes.
C-5 requires valid K12 names containing non-NUL C0 characters to be escaped exactly.
The pinned predicate admits a-space, a-LF and a-CR, all well within V; the new unconditional suffix refusal rejects each.

requiredFindings.fix: Keep no trimming and true whole-decoded-value matching for every grammar. Scope trailing-LF/CR/space rejection to identities, code members and other grammars that actually exclude them. Explicitly preserve lawful K12 path/tail suffixes, encoded by E, in the common rule and r4 response table. Add positive C-4/C-5 writer/read-back cases for path and elided-tail values ending in space, LF and CR, while retaining the existing negative suffix cases for RequestId, identities, K1 and K14.
